input: read ./prompt.md and follow the instructions there
task: Explore (free choice): new GTFS transit feed checker, ventures/gtfs-feed-check
errors: First calendar-coverage pass clipped dates outside a two-year window, so Google's 2007 sample showed no service dates and the broken example's first date read 2024-11-19; fixed with first/last running day of out-of-window ranges, and a test pins it.
Per-row JS arrays for stop_times used ~670 MB heap on TriMet; switched to columnar typed arrays (339 MB including the raw text).
Page copy said 'fourteen kinds of problem'; the test that counts them found 17; copy fixed, test keeps it honest.
A literal U+FEFF in a test string tripped check_hidden_unicode; written as an escape.

doc_friction.issue: Definition of done names register-tool.mjs and venture-preflight.mjs but not that a new file-pre-flight venture lands in the full 'More free tools' catch-all and needs a slug line in platform/pages/build.mjs; preflight told me, after ~2 minutes.
Post title/description/seo_title limits (110/160/70) are only discovered by running the check; CLAUDE.md's post guidance does not state them.

deviations.why: Website requests and IDEAS.md were empty and the route drew explore, so the run picked its own idea.
deviations.did: Screened GTFS with duplicate_check.py (top 0.20), built a venture with real-feed evaluation.
deviations.result: Merged with 60 passing tests and a real-data post.

notes: Idea: GTFS Schedule feed checker (browser + CLI), first transit-data tool in the portfolio. Measured on Google's sample, BART, Halifax Transit and TriMet (hashes in eval). Sanity limits (speed, outliers) had zero hits on 3.0M real stop times. Mutation: 5 mutants tried, all caught after two boundary tests added. Chromium check: BART zip loads, no console errors, no external requests, 390 px no overflow. No separate docs/reports agent doc: README's depth path and VENTURE.yaml carry what the next run needs.

pricing.source: Anthropic pricing as cached in the Claude API skill (models table and per-model migration notes), 2026-10-06. Cache writes are 1.25x input (5-minute) and 2x input (1-hour); cache reads differ by model.

human_equivalent.basis: estimate: a developer writing a GTFS checker (88 rules, zip reader, CLI, two pages, tests, real-feed eval) from the spec

certainty.tokens: high: summed from the per-request `usage` the API returned, as the transcript recorded it, deduplicated by message id
certainty.model: high: the `model` field on each API response, not the configured model
certainty.api_equivalent_usd: medium: measured tokens x list prices in prompts/pricing.json (as_of stated); an equivalent, not a charge: these runs are billed under a subscription
certainty.time: medium: from transcript timestamps; model time is request-to-response, tool time is call-to-result, time waiting on a person is excluded from active time
certainty.human_equivalent: low: the agent's own estimate of how long a competent person would take, with its basis written down; never measured

not_counted: requests the harness makes outside the transcript (context compaction summaries, title generation, safety classifiers), if any
transcripts lost when a cloud session moved to a new container: only files present in this container are read, so a resumed session can undercount
server-tool fees (web search is billed per search, not per token); the count is recorded, not priced
CI minutes and the reviewer bots' own model calls
